publicNotes.title: Somatic Inquiry List
publicNotes.excerpt: Experiences and patterns I may want to bring into a self-guided somatic inquiry session.
publicNotes.bodyMarkdown:
# Somatic Inquiry List

Things I notice in life that may be useful to investigate during a self-guided somatic inquiry session, sometimes with cannabis. These are prompts, not conclusions about what they mean or where they came from.

## What I’ve noticed

- Fear of being judged
- Self-consciousness
- Embarrassment when I do something ‘wrong’
- Thinking too much in terms of perceived value
- Thinking too much in terms of status and hierarchy

## Other things to explore

- What happens in my body when I’m visible, evaluated, criticized, or misunderstood?
- The urge to explain or defend an unconventional view
- Feeling that I need to get something exactly right before sharing it
- The relationship between worth and usefulness, productivity, intelligence, appearance, or status
- The impulse to optimize, fix, research, or collect another technique instead of staying with the experience
- What stability, rootedness, and commitment bring up after years of prioritizing freedom and mobility
- What happens when I don’t know, can’t control the outcome, or have to wait
- Receiving help, attention, appreciation, or care without needing to earn it
- Conflict between trusting my own perception and wanting external confirmation
- The felt difference between genuine curiosity and anxious searching
- Whether embarrassment is protecting me from being playful, strange, earnest, or fully seen
- The point at which independence becomes isolation

## Session notes

- What was the trigger or situation?
- Where is it felt in the body?
- What happens when I stay with sensation without explaining it?
- What impulse, image, memory, movement, or emotion appears?
- What feels unfinished?
- What changes, even slightly?
